problem_statement: wpcodevo/lc28-fashion-ecommerce-website is a runnable static HTML5/CSS/JS fashion storefront (Boxicons + SwiperJS, served directly from static files) whose collection section renders a catalog-backed product carousel and its OWN category filter (the .filters chip row: Jewellery / Accessories / Dresses / Footwear) driven by data/products.json — clicking a chip re-renders the collection grid to that category. The store's shop-by-category browsing is completed here so a shopper can always tell what they are looking at: (1) a live count readout beneath the native filter chips (class 'shopfilter__readout', id #shopfilter-readout) reading 'Showing N of 16 · <Category>' that stays in sync with the filtered collection grid; (2) a shared 'Browse the collection' summary label (class 'shopfilter-summary') that appears on any page so the merchandising language is consistent site-wide; and (3) two companion pages, lookbook.html and checkout.html, that reuse the same header nav and the summary label. The filter row + readout are styled by a dedicated stylesheet css/shopfilter.css and the live-count wiring is in js/shopfilter.js (which only hooks the repo's existing selectCategory; js/product.js is untouched). In the current build FOUR things are wrong and must be repaired together while keeping the same catalog, native filter, carousel and storefront look: (A) the filter chip row uses a fixed pixel width with flex-wrap:nowrap and fixed-width chips, so on a 390px phone the chips cannot wrap and push the home document wider than the viewport (a horizontal scrollbar appears) while desktop and tablet look fine; (B) the shared 'Browse the collection' summary label must appear on the home page, the lookbook page AND the checkout page, not just some of them; (C) the filtered collection grid must keep the storefront's warm orange / white rounded-card palette and clean grid geometry, not collapse into a dark charcoal pile of overlapping cards; and (D) clicking a category chip must update the live readout to 'Showing N of 16 · <Category>' for that category, not leave it frozen on the previous category. The fixes must live in the filter/readout layout+palette (css/shopfilter.css) and the live-count wiring (js/shopfilter.js) plus the shared summary-label placement across the three pages; do not touch the product catalog, the Swiper carousel behaviour, the native selectCategory in js/product.js, the load-more grid, the login modal, or the storefront visual language.
required_content: The collection keeps the repo's OWN native category filter (the .filters chip row Jewellery / Accessories / Dresses / Footwear) driving the real #products grid from data/products.json, and gains a live count readout (#shopfilter-readout) reading 'Showing N of 16 · <Category>'.
The home page (index.html) no longer overflows horizontally at 390px: the filter chip row and collection grid wrap or shrink so the document width equals the phone viewport width.
The shared 'Browse the collection' summary label (class 'shopfilter-summary') is present on the home page, the lookbook page and the checkout page.

The native filter row, the readout and the collection grid keep the storefront's orange / white rounded soft-shadow cards and on-brand typography (no dark/charcoal off-palette collapse or overlapping card pile).

Clicking a category chip filters the collection grid AND updates the live readout to 'Showing N of 16 · <Category>' for that category; the terminal state after a Footwear click reads 'Showing 3 of 16 · Footwear', not a stale 'Showing 3 of 16 · Dresses'.
Desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) layouts of the filter row, readout and collection carousel are visually preserved with no new overflow.

The collection carousel, native category filter, load-more grid, login modal, navigation and footer remain functional and reachable; the data/products.json catalog and local product image assets continue to drive the product surfaces.
No JavaScript console errors or failed network requests are introduced on any captured state.
design_constraints: Match the existing orange gradient, white card surfaces, box shadows, rounded product cards, centered section spacing, and fashion storefront typography for the filter row, readout and summary label.
The filter + readout should read as the collection's own shop-by-category affordance, not a full hero replacement, modal, dashboard widget, or separate app shell.
The collection product cards must keep a clean grid, keep product images visible, and avoid overlapping or piling on top of each other.
The filter chip row must become responsive (wrap onto multiple rows and/or use a flexible chip basis) rather than relying on a fixed pixel row width with non-wrapping fixed-width chips.
Do not mask the overflow by clipping the row with overflow-x:hidden or shrinking the row width while keeping chips/cards from wrapping; the document itself must not exceed the mobile viewport.
The shared summary label must be a genuinely site-wide affordance: the SAME label on home, lookbook and checkout, not present on some pages and missing on others.
The live-count wiring must re-read the filtered grid on every category change; a handler that filters the grid but leaves the readout frozen on the previous category is not acceptable.
Desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile states must avoid horizontal overflow and text overlap.

Only css/shopfilter.css and js/shopfilter.js and the shared summary-label placement change between the broken and repaired build; the product markup, catalog data, native selectCategory, and other sections stay the same.
state_constraints: desktop_home captures index.html at 1440px: the native category filter, the live 'Showing 3 of 16 · Dresses' readout and the 'Browse the collection' summary label render on-brand with no horizontal overflow.

mobile_home / mobile_collection capture the same page at 390px, where the broken fixed-width nowrap filter row + collapsed grid push the document wider than the viewport; the repaired filter removes that overflow.
desktop_collection / mobile_collection scroll the collection grid + native filter into the viewport so their on-brand palette and grid geometry are judged visually (this is the D3 host).

desktop_filter_footwear / mobile_filter_footwear click the native Footwear category chip and confirm the collection grid re-renders AND the live readout updates to 'Showing 3 of 16 · Footwear'; the mobile filter state must also be free of horizontal overflow after the repair.
desktop_filter_footwear is the interaction terminal state: after clicking Footwear the readout must read 'Showing 3 of 16 · Footwear', changed from 'Showing 3 of 16 · Dresses' on desktop_collection.
desktop_lookbook / desktop_checkout load the two companion pages and confirm the shared 'Browse the collection' summary label is present cross-page.
desktop_login_modal opens the existing login modal to confirm the extension did not regress the modal or navigation scripts.

Source inspection confirms the site is a static HTML template served directly; the native .filters chip row + selectCategory live in js/product.js (untouched), css/shopfilter.css controls the filter row + readout + grid layout/palette, and js/shopfilter.js hooks selectCategory to keep the #shopfilter-readout count in sync.

change_completion: The mobile home page no longer overflows horizontally: document width equals the 390px viewport within tolerance.
The collection keeps its native category filter and gains a live 'Showing N of 16 · <Category>' readout; clicking Footwear updates the readout to 'Showing 3 of 16 · Footwear'.
The shared 'Browse the collection' summary label is present on the home, lookbook and checkout pages.
design_consistency: The filter row, readout and collection grid keep the orange gradient, white rounded soft-shadow cards, and on-brand typography (no dark charcoal off-palette collapse).
Desktop and tablet appearance of the filter, readout and collection carousel is preserved.
The page remains the same fashion storefront, not a redesigned layout.
regression: The collection carousel, native category filter, load-more grid, login modal, navigation, and footer remain functional and reachable.
The data/products.json catalog and product image assets continue to drive the product surfaces.
No console errors or failed requests are introduced on any captured state.
responsive: 390px home, collection and filter states have no horizontal overflow, card collisions, or clipped cards.
The filter chip row and collection grid wrap or shrink cleanly on mobile while staying tidy on desktop/tablet.

author_notes: Repo-grounded static lc28-fashion-ecommerce storefront (wpcodevo). L4 harden of the store's OWN native shop-by-category browsing: the existing .filters chip row + selectCategory over the collection carousel, completed with a live 'Showing N of 16 · <Category>' count readout, a shared 'Browse the collection' summary label, and two companion pages (lookbook.html, checkout.html) that reuse the header nav + label. Content and DOM are byte-identical across reference/baseline/bad; the only source that varies between legs is css/shopfilter.css, js/shopfilter.js and the summary-label placement across the three pages (js/product.js stays pristine). Four orthogonal discriminators: no_horizontal_overflow (tol 24) on the mobile collection/filter states (reference 0px, baseline +390px, bad +250px); cross-page dom_assertions for the shared summary label (present on home/lookbook/checkout); visual_regression on the scrolled collection states (the bad negative-margin collapse piles the real product cards into an illegible near-black heap); and interaction_assertions on the post-click readout (bad filters the grid but leaves the readout stale). Vendored Boxicons/Swiper assets and local product imagery keep all three legs runtime-clean (0 console, 0 network, 0 overflow on the reference) across the ten captured states.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: lc28-fashion-ecommerce-website is a runnable static fashion storefront whose collection already ships a native category filter over data/products.json; used here to complete the store's own shop-by-category browsing with a live count readout, a site-wide summary label, and companion pages, whose responsive layout, cross-page consistency, on-brand palette and interaction terminal state are the deterministic product-grade discriminators.
metadata.defect: native category filter chip row uses a fixed-width nowrap row that causes mobile horizontal overflow; the shared summary label is inconsistent across pages; a charcoal negative-margin collapse piles the collection cards illegibly; and the live-count readout stays frozen on the previous category
metadata.discriminator: no_horizontal_overflow (tol 24, mobile) + cross-page summary-label dom_assertions + visual_regression on the collection states + category-filter interaction_assertions
